svg.title: Four Gates Before a Shipper Earns More Freight
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-shipper-qualification-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Four Gates Before a Shipper Earns More Freight; subtitle: Vetting, margin floor, payment terms and pipeline discipline, per Dennis Brown; chart type: decision_tree; caption: Brown's startup rules - vet every party, hold a $100 floor, state 30-day terms, and keep 90%+ of time on prospecting - protect cash while 5-10 shippers build a six-figure book.; assumptions note: Gate order is an editorial sequence. Each threshold is quoted from FreightBrokers sessions led by Dennis Brown.; note: Source - FreightBrokers with Dennis Brown (UhCy0ncTrTI, j9lUdJynzFA, dciVQpw-BWM, kc6-g1EZ0Fk).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Has due diligence cleared the shipper, the carrier and the driver?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold the tender until all three checks are complete.; gate: G2; question: Does the load clear $100 gross while targeting 10-15% margin?; pass next: G3; fail action: After the deliberate break-even first load, drop shippers below $100 gross.; gate: G3; question: Were 30-day terms stated upfront and AP called after the first load?; pass next: G4; fail action: Trigger a credit hold at 60 days unpaid.; gate: G4; question: Is 90% or more of time still spent prospecting as loads arrive?; pass next: Grow toward 5-10 active small-to-midsize shippers.; fail action: Rebuild the pipeline; the business dies when prospecting stops.

text.title: Four Gates Before a Shipper Earns More Freight
text.tspan: Four Gates Before a Shipper Earns More Freight

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Has due diligence cleared the shipper, the carrier and the driver?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold the tender until all three checks are complete.
gate: G2; question: Does the load clear $100 gross while targeting 10-15% margin?; pass next: G3; fail action: After the deliberate break-even first load, drop shippers below $100 gross.
gate: G3; question: Were 30-day terms stated upfront and AP called after the first load?; pass next: G4; fail action: Trigger a credit hold at 60 days unpaid.

gate: G4; question: Is 90% or more of time still spent prospecting as loads arrive?; pass next: Grow toward 5-10 active small-to-midsize shippers.; fail action: Rebuild the pipeline; the business dies when prospecting stops.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is an editorial sequence. Each threshold is quoted from FreightBrokers sessions led by Dennis Brown.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order is an editorial sequence. Each threshold is quoted from FreightBrokers sessions led by Dennis Brown.
